title: The Saline Testimony Chamber

features.name: salt-preserved witness
features.desc-on-touch: An old register or ledger, pages preserved in salt crust. The ink has faded but the words beneath remain—testimony from someone who lived near the water a long time. You can almost taste salt reading it.

features.name: keeper's station
features.desc-on-touch: A small structure, whitewashed and weathered. Inside, jars of salt, containers of water samples, implements of preservation. A life spent recording what the tide brings.

features.name: crystalline archive
features.desc-on-touch: Salt residue arranged in patterns, some natural, some intentional. The patterns form letters, or possibly memories in mineral form. Time crystallized.

features.name: tidal measure
features.desc-on-touch: A device of wood and salt-corroded metal, marking the high- and low-water lines. The gaps between marks are growing. The water is speaking in long sentences now.

features.name: brine-pool
features.desc-on-touch: Water so saturated it seems to hold everything that ever dissolved into it. You see faces in it, places, names written in salt script that fades as you read.

inscription: salt keeps what it touches, and touches everything

file.name: UnknownWitness_LogEntry_1963_SaltPreserved.txt
file.note: Personal testimony, possibly from a salt-yard keeper or civic recorder. Increasingly fragmentary. Final entry: 'The water remembers better than I do. I am learning its language.' Subsequent pages blan
